summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported that Charley Gallagher beat the favorite Tom Allen at Carroll's Island, Illinois, knocking him unconscious in the second round with a right under the left ear.

metadata.notes: Masthead 'Daily Democrat', Wednesday morning, Feb. 24, 1869. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen lost to Charley Gallagher at Carroll's Island, Illinois, opposite Quarantine station twelve miles below St. Louis, knocked out of time in the second round by a right-hand blow on the neck under the left ear
places: Carroll's Island, Illinois, opposite Quarantine, below St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen was the betting favorite at three to two; he lay unconscious about five minutes after the knockout
Impatient at the delay in choosing a referee, Allen threw off his blankets and told Gallagher he would fight without one
facts.quote: I will fight you without a referee—you rotten cur!

facts.fact: After coming to, Allen said he was sorry for his backers, had never felt so confident of winning, and would fight Gallagher again immediately or in a week for any amount
The paper gave Allen as 28 years old, 5 feet 9 inches tall and 168 pounds, an English fighter

The paper listed Allen's English record: beat Morris Conner (June 1861), White, Clark and Jack Gould (1862, Birmingham district); lost to Posh Price (1862); beat Bingey Rose (London district); lost to Bob Smith in Liverpool (1863, 108 rounds); beat Jack Parkinson (1863), Posh Price (1864) and George Iles (1866); and beat Bill Davis last month
